deviations_from_card: Acceptance case 5 (report Metrics bullets, moment recall) is the new case 9 in tools/uat-recertify-test.cjs (the card says to reuse that harness); cases 1-4, 6, 7 are in tools/uat-metrics-test.cjs. Case 8 (guards: uat-verdict-test case 6 and uat-recertify-test case 2) is the two untouched existing tests, so tools/uat-verdict-test.cjs is not edited. cases_red_before 6 = cases 2,3,4,5,6,7; the guards are case 1 (new, snapshot of the pre-change schema) and case 8 (existing). The first commit (867e65e2) is red by design (the registry file did not exist), declared as such in its message; every later commit is green. The refactor landed as 3 commits (registry+verdict+recertify, then linga-text+rubric, then the package.json wiring under the lock) rather than 2. The rubric.md edit adds one paragraph naming the two driver-measured rows and the gateable series ids (needed for case 7).
notes: User-visible changes beyond the card: (1) report.md gains a 'moment recall' bullet, and the per-Character report's Metrics line gains 'moment recall n/d (p%)' (the card lists the bullet; the per-Character line is the same registry loop). (2) metricDelta() gains an eighth key, 'recall', which recertify.md's Metric deltas table now prints; it is marked informative so a fall in recall is never listed under Regressed (rubric: 'informative, not gated'); the card says the existing seven keys are unchanged, and they are. (3) 'agreement' and 'recall' are now gateable ids (judge agreement could not be gated before); no committed journey gates them. (4) parseArgs() now reads journey files and throws on an unknown gate metric in every mode except --status, so a typo stops the run before any spawn; the error names the journey and metric and lists the known ids. Instrument hash: metrics.cjs is added to instrumentOf()'s driver hash list, so a run recorded after this commit differs from an earlier run's instrument by one new driver entry and metrics.cjs will show in the recertify 'instrument changed' confound, as any driver change does (this is the intended behaviour of that confound). Placement stays a tally entry: its series reads class counts from the roll-up, and its gate still reads record.facts.placement.class as before. Recall is defined as (learnerTurnsWithClearErrors - missedClearErrors) over learnerTurnsWithClearErrors, per the rubric; over the committed runs the bullets would read 3/61 (5%), 22/43 (51%) etc, not asserted by any test. The 'check length' rubric row is named driver-measured; nothing counts it in code (the card only asked for it to be named). Judge schema is byte-identical (JSON string equality, key order included) for ([],[]) and (['x'],['D1','D2']); every committed report's six existing Metrics bullets reproduce from the registry roll-up (checked by script, not a test). No TV screen touched, no capture needed. No disagreement with the scout's design; one note: the registry also lets a second module register a metric with its own schema, but the report/judge prompts still say Linga (premise 8 is untouched by design).
